items.text: Dan Quinn ruled Jayden Daniels (WAS) out Friday for the London game vs IND; the dislocated left elbow gets a full week of practice before Washington decides on Week 5. Marcus Mariota makes his second straight start after every snap and 3 touchdowns vs SEA. Mariota is QB19 for me, a streamer, and Daniels managers pivot to him or any QB in my top 18.

items.watch: Washington's final injury report Friday; an out or doubtful makes Croskey-Merritt the lead back
items.text: Rachaad White (WAS) did not practice Friday in London either, three straight missed sessions with the shoulder he hurt vs SEA. Jacory Croskey-Merritt played 57 percent of the snaps with 19 carries Sunday and has 58 percent of Washington's carries, with Austin Ekeler on the receiving downs. Croskey-Merritt is RB24 for me this week, an RB2. White: monitor Washington's final injury report Friday.

Aaron Glenn ruled Breece Hall (NYJ) out Friday with the quad, along with Adonai Mitchell (finger). Braelon Allen played every snap after Hall left at DET, and Isaiah Davis has no offensive snap this season. Allen is RB21 for me this week, an RB2 @CHI.

items.watch: the Jets' Friday designation; questionable with a full Friday keeps him TE12
items.text: The Jets ruled Mason Taylor (NYJ) out Friday with the thumb, his second straight missed game. Kenyon Sadiq was limited Wednesday and Thursday with the back; at DET he ran a route on 58 percent of the dropbacks and drew 8 of 37 targets, 7 for 105. He is TE12 for me, a borderline start this week. Monitor Sadiq; the Friday designation.

New Orleans put Travis Etienne Jr. (NO) on IR Thursday with the hamstring, so he is out at least four games and Week 8 is the earliest return. After Etienne left in Week 3, Alvin Kamara took 6 of the next 10 carries and 20 of 34 second-half snaps, with Kendre Miller next and CJ Donaldson on short yardage. Kamara is RB25 for me vs ATL, a high-end RB3, a high-end flex play.

Lamar Jackson (BAL) practiced in full Thursday after a limited Wednesday with the back, and Jesse Minter called it something small. Both centers are still out, so a rookie guard snaps to him. The Menu flag comes off; he stays QB2 for me vs TEN.

Mike Evans (SF) missed Thursday's practice too and worked on the side with the ribs; general manager John Lynch said he will make every attempt to play vs DEN. He left the ARI game in the second quarter after the hit and is not ranked on the Menu until he practices. Monitor; Friday's practice line and designation.

Justin Jefferson (MIN) was officially a non-participant Thursday, his second straight missed practice with the ankle sprain; Friday is his last chance before a designation vs MIA. When he left at TB the targets went to Jordan Addison first, 9 of Kyler Murray's 29 attempts, 5 for 90 and a touchdown. Addison is WR31 for me, a low-end WR3, a low-end flex play, with more room if Jefferson sits. Monitor Jefferson; Friday practice and the designation.
items.watch: Friday practice and the game designation

items.text: Tony Pollard (TEN) practiced in full Thursday after a Wednesday DNP with the foot, while Tyjae Spears (ankle) was limited. Pollard had 53 percent of the snaps and 80 percent of the early downs at NYG with no third-down snap. His flag comes off. RB28 for me, a high-end RB3, a flex play @BAL.

DJ Moore (BUF) was limited Wednesday and Thursday with the shoulder, the same as last week, when he played and drew a team-high 10 targets, 6 for 67, on 64 percent of the snaps vs LAC. The Menu rows keep the flag. WR24 for me this week, a WR2 vs NE.

Bucky Irving (TB) was limited again Thursday with the glute he hurt on the last two drives vs MIN. He is RB19 for me this week, an RB2, with a rookie quarterback handing off vs GB. Monitor; Friday's practice line and designation, and have a backup ready.

Zay Flowers (BAL) practiced in full Thursday after a limited Wednesday with the hamstring, so the 21-snap pitch count from Brazil should lift. On 26 routes this season he has 234 yards and a target on 48 percent of them. The flag comes off; WR8 for me vs TEN.

Tyjae Spears (TEN) was limited Thursday after a Wednesday DNP with the ankle; last week he did not practice until Friday. He runs more routes than Tony Pollard and owns the third downs when active. Monitor Spears; Friday's practice line and designation.

Christian Watson (GB) was not on Wednesday's injury report and was not mentioned Thursday, so the hamstring listing after Week 3 did not carry into Week 4. He has 24 percent of the targets, 80 percent of the routes and a touchdown in every game, and Jayden Reed is on IR. WR11 for me, borderline WR1/WR2 this week at TB.

items.price: a flex-level receiver, or a bench back with a clearer path
items.text: Seattle opened Zach Charbonnet's 21-day practice window Thursday; he must sit the first four games, so Week 5 is the earliest he plays, and he takes the short-yardage, goal-line and pass-protection snaps when active. Jadarian Price (SEA) had 6 touches on 19 snaps at WAS, third of the three backs, with 2 lost fumbles on 32 touches. RB30 for me, a high-end RB3 by rank and a sit vs LAC. Trade him away now; ask for a flex-level receiver.

Zach Charbonnet (SEA) is back at practice off reserve/PUP with the window open Thursday; the ACL was in the January playoff, Week 5 is the earliest he can play, and Seattle can activate him any time in 21 days. The backfield he returns to is a three-way rotation, Emanuel Wilson 24 snaps, George Holani 24 and Price 19 at WAS, with no back over 9 carries. Stash him, 3 to 5 percent of FAAB, where he is available.

Colston Loveland (CHI) has 9 targets, 5 catches and 34 yards in three games (0, 3 and 31 by week) on 71 percent of the routes, while slot receiver Kalif Raymond has 21 targets and a team-high 214 yards, and Chicago has still not named a quarterback for Sunday. The Menu has him TE14, a streamer at best. TE14 for me, borderline by rank, and the lean is sit for any tight end with a target share above 15 percent.

Jaylen Waddle (DEN) wore a walking boot after the win at LAR as a precaution, then practiced in full Wednesday, and Sean Payton says he is fine. He ran 82 percent of the routes and drew 7 targets in that game, 2 catches for 10. WR21 for me this week, a WR2 at SF.

Both of Green Bay's starting guards, Aaron Banks (knee, toe) and Jacob Monk (quad), missed Wednesday and Thursday, and the two veterans signed this week, Laken Tomlinson and Kevin Zeitler, took the first-team work Thursday with Mekhi Becton on the practice squad. Jordan Love (GB) has been hit 20 times in three games on a league-low 2.4 seconds to throw, and the run game is last in the league at 48.7 yards a game, so the volume (124 attempts) stays. QB12 for me, a borderline start this week at TB.

DeVonta Smith (PHI) did not practice Thursday, his second straight DNP with the hamstring, the same arc as last week when he missed Wednesday and Thursday, went limited Friday and played every snap at CHI. He has 33 percent of the targets on the season and is WR10 on the Menu with the flag. If he sits, Dontayvion Wicks is WR42 for me, a low-end flex play to a dart throw. Monitor; a limited or full Friday means he plays.
items.watch: Friday practice line and the designation

items.text: Dallas Goedert (PHI) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday with the sprained MCL, still week to week with no timeline and no IR move. Johnny Mundt (26 snaps, 10 routes) and Zach Ertz (19 snaps, 11 routes) split the job at CHI and neither drew more than 2 targets, so neither is a play. He stays off the Menu with Juwan Johnson as the pivot. Monitor; Friday's designation.
items.watch: Friday's designation; an out keeps the Juwan Johnson pivot

items.text: Nico Collins (HOU) practiced again Thursday after a limited Wednesday, his first two sessions since the hamstring strain that cost him Weeks 2 and 3, and he is trending toward playing vs DAL. While he was out nobody in the receiver room played 70 percent of the snaps, so the share comes back to him whole. WR12 for me, borderline WR1/WR2 this week, and the flag stays until Friday's designation; carry a backup.

Chris Godwin (TB) returned to practice Thursday after sitting out Wednesday with the ankle; the participation level was not posted. He had slipped to 62 percent of the snaps vs MIN, third among the receivers behind Ted Hurst III, 3 for 25, and he has 10 catches for 111 on the season. WR57 for me, a dart throw; sit him for any receiver inside my top 36 whether or not he plays.

Mack Hollins (NE) leads the Patriots with 16 targets through three games (5, 2, 9) to DeMario Douglas' 14 and Romeo Doubs' 11, and Doubs has not had a game above 4. A.J. Brown is on IR since Sep 11 and eligible to return Week 6, not Week 7, so the volume is open for two more games at least. Hollins is not ranked on the Menu. Add him, 2 to 5 percent of FAAB.

Darren Waller (CAR) led Carolina with 8 targets on 28 routes and 39 of 77 snaps at CLE, 5 catches for 51, with Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette out. Coker (quad) was upgraded to limited Thursday after a Wednesday DNP and a game-time decision is possible; Legette did not practice. Waller is outside the Menu's top 20 tight ends, so this is a streamer's call. Monitor Coker's Friday designation; Waller is a stream vs DET only if Coker is out.

The London forecast for IND at WAS (Sunday 9:30 AM ET) has moved from a 90 percent chance of rain on Wednesday to mostly dry, high 60s, wind under 10 miles an hour, by Thursday morning. Josh Downs (IND) has 3, 9 and 11 targets since Alec Pierce went on IR, and he is WR17 for me this week, a WR2; the call was the targets, not the weather. Tyler Warren is TE4 for me.

Ladd McConkey (LAC) was limited Wednesday with a foot injury, a new listing; the cracked rib held him to 49 and 46 percent of the snaps in Weeks 1 and 2 before he played 88 percent at BUF, 4 of 5 for 66. The Menu row now carries the flag and he stays WR20. Start him as a WR2 at SEA if Thursday's line says limited or full, and have a backup ready for Friday's designation.

Cleveland ruled center Elgton Jenkins (concussion) out for Thursday night vs PIT, so Luke Wypler starts in the middle, and Tylan Wallace (knee) and guard Teven Jenkins (back) are out too. Quinshon Judkins (CLE) has 42 carries for 124 yards, 3.0 a carry, with no touchdown, and ran 11 routes to Raheim Sanders' 16 last week. Flex Judkins vs PIT; he is not an RB2 behind that line.

items.watch: Thursday and Friday practice lines and the Friday designation
items.text: Puka Nacua (LAR) practiced Wednesday as a limited participant, his first session in about two weeks with the groin, and Sean McVay said he expects him to play at PHI. Davante Adams drew 13 targets at DEN without him. Nacua is not on the Menu; the Friday run ranks him if he practices Thursday. Monitor; Thursday's and Friday's practice lines and the Friday designation.

Keon Coleman (BUF) did not practice Wednesday with the ankle that had him questionable last week, when he played 48 percent of the snaps vs LAC and caught 1 of 2 for 37. DJ Moore drew a team-high 10 targets in that game. Joshua Palmer gets the snaps if Coleman sits. Sit Coleman vs NE either way.

Ashton Jeanty (LV) is on Wednesday's report with the ankle he had taped at NO and practiced in full. He has 20 or more touches in every game and 16 targets, and Mike Washington Jr. has 15 carries for 102 behind him. Start Jeanty as an RB1 vs KC.

Aaron Jones Sr. (MIN) was listed limited Wednesday as a rest day, not injury related, so the knee from Week 2 is off the report. He has 78 percent of the carries and a 24 percent target share since Jordan Mason went on IR, and MIA has allowed the most points to running backs. Start him as your RB2 vs MIA.

Drake Maye (NE) was added to the injury report Wednesday with the right shoulder and practiced in full; he says it has not affected his arm or his decisions. The line is the problem: 1 touchdown pass, 6 interceptions and 9 sacks in three games, under 13 fantasy points in each. Sit him at BUF.

Rico Dowdle (PIT) was ruled out Wednesday for Thursday night at CLE with the toe; he did not practice all week and his right foot was in a walking boot. Jaylen Warren played 90 percent of the snaps and had 20 touches the last time Dowdle sat, and Pittsburgh ran two tight ends on most snaps vs CIN, so the checkdowns run through him. Start Warren as an RB1.

Ben Johnson said Wednesday the Bears have picked their starter vs NYJ and will not say whether it is Tyson Bagent (CHI) or Case Keenum; Bagent is cleared from the concussion and Caleb Williams (hamstring) sat out the walkthrough. Keenum threw for the win at PHI on Monday night. Neither is a fantasy start. Monitor; the Friday practice report and the Sunday inactives for who takes first-team reps.
items.watch: Friday practice report and Sunday inactives

items.text: At JAX the early downs were an even split, and Rhamondre Stevenson, not TreVeyon Henderson (NE), took most of the passing-situation and short-yardage snaps: 33 snaps to 23 and 3 catches to 1. The passing-down case for Henderson does not hold this week. Sit him at BUF; Stevenson stays a RB2.

Mack Hollins drew 9 targets (6 for 87) at JAX to Romeo Doubs' 4 (3 for 49) and led the New England receivers in snaps, so Hollins is the A.J. Brown pivot on the Menu and Doubs (NE) comes down from a WR3. Doubs has 6 catches for 145 in the two games without Brown, 3 catches in each. Flex Doubs; do not start him as a WR3.

Justin Jefferson did not practice Wednesday, and Kyler Murray (MIN) went 15 of 29 for 168 yards with 3 sacks at TB in an offense that scored one touchdown; the defense and special teams won the game. He comes off the Menu's stream line. Sit him vs MIA unless Jefferson practices by Friday.

Jaylen Wright (MIA) was limited at Wednesday's practice with the foot after sitting out Week 3, and he had been working ahead of Ollie Gordon II before he was hurt. Jeff Hafley says every back will have a role. Wright has 3 carries this season. Stash him, 5 to 10 percent of FAAB; Thursday and Friday decide whether he is back in the split at MIN.

Tre' Harris (LAC) had his best game, 6 of 7 for 76 vs BUF, on his smallest snap share of the season: 58 percent after 75 and 82, because Ladd McConkey came back to 88 percent of the snaps and Quentin Johnston played 87. The targets grew while the role shrank, so he moves from the Market Run adds to the stashes. Stash him, 1 to 3 percent of FAAB; he needs a starter to miss time.

DK Metcalf (PIT) had 5 targets vs CIN even with Roman Wilson benched for the second half, and he has 98 yards on 24 targets in three games while Pittsburgh leaned on two tight ends (Darnell Washington 47 of 62 snaps). The targets did not consolidate, so both Menu lists now say the same thing. Flex him at CLE Thursday; he is not a WR3 start.

Jadarian Price (SEA) had 6 touches on 19 snaps and 11 routes at WAS, third of the three backs in carries and routes, and his fumble came on his third carry with no carry again until the third quarter; he has 2 lost fumbles on 32 touches. Mike Macdonald said Monday the team keeps giving him the ball, but the usage does not support a flex yet. Sit him vs LAC until the first-quarter carries come back.

Emeka Egbuka (TB) has 13 catches for 141 on 20 targets in three games, and his snap share fell from 86 to 74 percent vs MIN while Baker Mayfield was sacked 6 times behind this line; undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels starts vs GB. The Menu's receiver list said start and the flex list said sit; both now say flex. Flex him vs GB, and sit him in 10-team leagues.

Wan'Dale Robinson (TEN) drew a game-high 11 targets at NYG, 7 for 57 and a touchdown, on 29 routes, 81 percent of the dropbacks. The Heat Check and the Menu said his snaps went from 28 to 38; a second snap source has 36, so both pages now cite the route share instead. Claim him, 2 to 5 percent of FAAB; a PPR flex at BAL if the routes hold.

Matt LaFleur said Wednesday that Jayden Reed (GB) will have neck surgery and miss the rest of 2026, and Reed went on injured reserve the same day. An IR slot buys nothing in a redraft league now, and nobody inherits his job: the third receiver vs ATL was a three-man rotation, Skyy Moore 27 routes, J. Michael Sturdivant 19 and Bo Melton 19 on 55 dropbacks. Drop Reed in every redraft format.

Nico Collins (HOU) practiced Wednesday as a limited participant, his first session since the hamstring strain that cost him Weeks 2 and 3, and DeMeco Ryans is hopeful he plays vs DAL. He stays WR15 on the Menu with the Q flag, and Dallas has allowed 7 passing touchdowns in three games. Monitor Collins; Thursday's practice and Friday's designation decide it.

The Menu had David Montgomery (HOU) as an RB2 start off one game, 34 snaps to Woody Marks' 20 vs IND. Over three games the snaps are close to even: about level in Week 1, 42 to 38 in Week 2, then 34 to 20. Montgomery is at 2.8 yards a carry and has been hit at or behind the line on 68 percent of his runs, the highest rate in the league. Marks has more targets, 8 to 7. Both Menu lists now read the same. Flex Montgomery vs DAL; he is not an RB2 this week.

Woody Marks (HOU) has 8 targets and 50 routes in three games, and 37 percent of the snaps was Week 3 only; the split was about even in Week 1 and 42 to 38 in Week 2. His role grows when Houston trails, 6 targets in the 20-6 loss to CIN, and he took the goal-line score at IND. Flex him vs DAL in PPR.

Brian Thomas Jr. (JAX) ran 13 to 15 routes vs NE, under half of the dropbacks, on 23 of 62 snaps; he was on the field for 77 percent of the three-receiver snaps and off it in two-tight-end sets. Rookie Josh Cameron matched his 23 snaps and scored. The Menu had Thomas as a flex while the Market Run and Heat Check said drop; the Menu row now reads sit. Sit him @CIN, and in 12-team leagues cut him for any add on the Market Run list.

Jake Ferguson (DAL) is TE15 on the Menu and the row now reads sit instead of stream. His snap share went 76, 60 and 69 percent by week while Brevyn Spann-Ford went 22, 38 and 38, he is fifth on his own team with 11 targets, and he lost a fumble on the opening drive vs BAL. The 3 touchdowns are the whole line, and the Butcher Shop already has him as a sell. Sit him @HOU for any tight end with a steadier target share.

Keenan Allen (IND) faces possible league discipline after a September charge from an August arrest; league policy carries a three-game minimum, none has been announced, the next court date is Oct 26 and he is eligible now. He has 20 targets on 75 routes, 26.7 percent, and took 9 of 36 attempts vs HOU. Claim him, 3 to 6 percent of FAAB, and know a ban could land in season.

Khalil Shakir (BUF) drew 3 targets and caught 1 for 6 yards on 73 percent of the snaps vs LAC while DJ Moore drew a team-high 10. The Menu row said the volume was coming his way; it did not. Sit him vs NE; he comes down the receiver list on Friday's Prep Notes.

Left guard Damien Lewis (CAR) has a UCL tear in his elbow and is out vs DET, so Corey Bullock makes his first start and Carolina has three backup linemen in front of Bryce Young, the most-pressured quarterback in the league at 47 percent of dropbacks. Young had his foot stepped on at CLE, did not miss a snap, and Dave Canales expects him to play. He stays QB12 on the Menu with 939 passing yards behind him; monitor Thursday and Friday practice for his foot and for Jalen Coker before you commit.
items.watch: Thursday and Friday practice for Young's foot and for Coker

items.text: Jeremiyah Love (ARI) out-snapped Tyler Allgeier for the first time in Week 3, 56 snaps (64 percent) to 31, after Allgeier led 60 to 43 percent in Weeks 1 and 2: 21 of the backs' 23 carries for 90, 5 of 5 targets for 19 and a receiving touchdown, 22 routes. Allgeier kept 3 of the 5 goal-line snaps, and the game was a 54-dropback trailing script. Start Love as your RB2 @NYG and watch the first-half split and the goal line.

Harold Fannin Jr. (CLE) drew 9 targets, a 30 percent share, with 45 percent of the air yards, 7 catches for 51 and 2 touchdowns vs CAR on 87 percent of the snaps and 77 percent of the routes; his targets have gone 3, 6, 9 by week. Jerry Jeudy ran 23 routes with no target. Start Fannin as your TE1 vs PIT on Thursday.

Kalif Raymond (CHI) has 23 percent of the targets on 66 percent of the routes and 214 receiving yards through three games, with 9 or more PPR points in each, on more than 60 percent of the snaps every week. The usage is real; the quarterback may change to Tyson Bagent, and the share was built with Case Keenum. Add him in PPR, 2 to 5 percent of FAAB, as a WR4 with a floor, not a starter until you see him with Bagent.

Mike Washington Jr. (LV) has 15 carries for 102 yards, 6.8 a carry, with 5 for 54 and a 36-yard touchdown @NO, and the coach has said twice that he earned more opportunities. He has no receiving role. Jeanty still has 81 percent of the backs' carries, so this is a handcuff with a rising early-down share, and the yards per carry back it. Stash him, 3 to 8 percent of FAAB, if you own Jeanty or have a deep bench.

John Harbaugh said Jameis Winston starts vs ARI and that J.J. McCarthy, acquired from MIN for a 2027 fifth-round pick, is the No. 2 while he learns the offense, since Jake Haener was waived the day of the trade. Malik Nabers (NYG) drew 27 percent of the targets in Winston's first start, a nor'easter with 22 team attempts, but caught 5 of 6 for 26 yards at an average depth of target of 1.0. Hold Nabers as a WR2 on volume; what changes the call is McCarthy taking the job, and Week 6 vs NO is the first realistic date for that.
items.why: 27 percent of the targets holds even with a 1.0 average depth of target; the call changes only if McCarthy takes the job, Week 6 vs NO at the earliest.
